subject: Temporary GPU pool hold & scheduled release for Pioneer pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary capacity hold for Pioneer pilot

Hi team,

Quick ask — Pioneer (Sam Park) has committed to a 6-week pilot that will need a predictable block of dedicated GPUs during business hours (US-PST) for load testing and model tuning. Sales wants a short-term guarantee we can hold capacity during their ramp window before they sign the PO.

Details: attached is the pilot SLA and a rough token/throughput forecast. Pioneer wants exclusive access to a 2x A100-equivalent slice from 08:00–18:00 PST Mon–Fri for two weeks starting on 2027-05-03, then drops to a 25% reserved buffer for the remaining 4 weeks.

Questions I need answered by EOD tomorrow:
- Can we place a temporary hold on a dedicated pool (no autoscale evictions) for that start window?
- What is the expected impact on other Dedicated customers during that hold (throughput/latency estimates)?
- If we agree, what internal approvals do we need (billing/ops/legal) and what exact wording should appear in the PO?

Soojin — assigning to you to coordinate ops and confirm feasibility. Dev / Jonas — can you run quick capacity impact sims? Jordan — I'll let you lead the external comms once we have feasibility.

Thanks,
Marissa
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot_sla_matrix.pdf (PDF), requested_gpu_window.csv (CSV)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity hold for Pioneer pilot

Thanks Marissa — reading through the forecast now. High level: a temporary hold is possible but we should scope two things before committing: the exact network/region affinity (Pioneer prefers us-west1), and whether we treat this as a hard reservation (no preemption) or soft (best-effort with early notice).

Prelim answers:
- We can carve out a dedicated slice from an existing enterprise pool for a 2-week hard hold if we take the resources offline for burst assignments. That will reduce available spare capacity for short-notice canaries.
- Impact: estimated 8–12% higher cold-start latencies for queued requests in the affected region during peak hours if other customers hit bursts; throughput for pinned tenants remains stable. I'll attach a short note from infra after the capacity sim.

Immediate ask for Dev/Jonas: please run a sim for the requested dates and include: token/sec distribution, peak tails (p99), and an eviction plan if we need to reclaim early.

I'll book a 30-min ops sync tomorrow at 10:30 PST to finalize.

Soojin
Head of Dedicated Ops

To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity hold for Pioneer pilot

Running sims now — preliminary results attached. Short summary:
- If we pin a 2x A100-equivalent slice for 08:00–18:00 PST, expected cluster utilization in us-west1 jumps by ~18% during the window.
- p50 latency impact for remaining shared tenants: negligible; p95 up ~7%, p99 up ~15% in our stress scenario.
- We can implement a soft-eviction policy: 48-hour notice + automated fallback to a compatible lower-capacity variant. Hard eviction (immediate reclaim) would require manual approvals and is disruptive.

Edge case to call out: Pioneer plans repeated model compiles during tuning which spiky-izes memory usage; recommend we ask for a short warmup period (24–48h) before the official start date.

Attached: requested_gpu_window_sim_results.txt (TXT).

Dev
Infra / Serving Runtime

---
On Apr 15, 2027, at 11:03, Soojin Lee wrote: (see above)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-16T10:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity hold for Pioneer pilot

Thanks — I ran an allocation impact model against active Dedicated commitments. Two important notes:
1) We have spare nodes in the target region that can cover the 2-week hard hold if we delay a planned maintenance (we'd need ops approval). That keeps existing customers at SLA but reduces our schedule slack for upcoming updates.
2) If Pioneer signs and converts the hold to a paid reservation within 10 business days, we can re-provision capacity with zero customer impact. If they don't, we should release the hold on the planned release date.

My recommendation: propose a formal "hold-and-release" in the PO with two clauses: a) guaranteed hold window (start/end dates), b) automatic release unless signed reservation within 10 business days of start. That gives incentives to convert while limiting long tail ops risk.

I'm comfortable with the warmup ask; it's a low-friction step.

Jonas
Capacity Planning

On Apr 15, 2027, at 14:20, Dev Patel wrote: (see above)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Park <sam@pioneer.ai>, procurement@pioneer.ai
Date: 2027-04-16T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity hold for Pioneer pilot

Looping in Pioneer to confirm commercial terms.

Sam — quick summary from our side: Operations can grant a 2x A100-equivalent dedicated hold for 2027-05-03 to 2027-05-14 (08:00–18:00 PST weekdays) with the following conditions:
- Redwood will treat the first 48 hours as warmup and will not count warmup usage against the pilot budget.
- If Pioneer signs a reservation (per attached PO draft) within 10 business days of the hold start, Redwood will convert the hold to a paid reserved slice. Otherwise the hold will be released on 2027-05-15 at 00:00 PST.
- Pioneer agrees to provide a 24-hour notice for any planned extended compile/tuning jobs outside the scheduled window.

Draft PO attached for your legal/procurement review (po-draft-pioneer.pdf). Can you confirm these terms by EOD Monday? If anything is blocking, let me know and I can loop in Contracts.

Thanks,
Jordan
Enterprise Sales

On Apr 16, 2027, at 10:31, Jonas Weber wrote: (see above)

From: Sam Park <sam@pioneer.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity hold for Pioneer pilot

Thanks, Jordan — Pioneer confirms the window and warmup terms. Procurement will review the PO and aim to return redlines by 2027-04-22. Two quick asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood provide a short runbook for any planned reclaim process (we want to understand what happens to queued work if the hold is released early).
2) Can you add an SLA appendix that clarifies expected p95/p99 during the reserved window? Even a short table will help us sign faster.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Sam
Head of ML Engineering, Pioneer AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-20T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity hold for Pioneer pilot — ops summary and next steps

Summary from ops:
- We will provision the hold as a hard reservation for the requested window (2027-05-03 through 2027-05-14, 08:00–18:00 PST).
- Warmup: allow 48 hours before the start where Pioneer can pre-load and compile models without counting toward pilot usage.
- Reclaim policy: automated soft-eviction will not trigger during the hold window. Early release requires a manual approval chain: Head of Dedicated Ops + Head of Sales + Finance signoff. We will provide a 2-hour manual notice to the Pioneer contact if reclamation is necessary for safety reasons.
- Deliverables: Dev to produce the runway/reclaim runbook; Jonas to add an SLA appendix (p95/p99 numbers) for the PO; Jordan to collect PO redlines and route to Contracts.

Action owners and target dates:
- Dev: runbook draft by 2027-04-22
- Jonas: SLA appendix by 2027-04-22
- Jordan: procurement follow-up and PO collection by 2027-04-23
- Soojin: final ops sign-off and schedule provisioning 2027-04-25

If there are no objections, I'll mark the capacity as "held pending PO" in our scheduling system on 2027-04-25 and pause the node maintenance window.

Soojin
Head of Dedicated Ops
